{"verdict":"approve","issuesFound":[],"riskNotes":"The change meets the issue. `isValidUrl` in src/url.js now parses the value and allows only the `http:` and `https:` protocols. The `javascript:`, `ftp:`, `data:` and `file:` schemes, bare hosts and non-string values all return 400 `{"error":"invalid url"}`. The new tests cover each of these, plus the mixed-case `JavaScript:` and `HTTPS://` cases and a check that a rejected URL isn't stored. I read the diff and ran small `node -e` checks; I didn't run `npm test` myself and relied on the verifier's pass. I found a few edge cases that don't block the merge.
- The raw `body.url` is stored, not the parsed or normalised form. WHATWG URL parsing strips embedded tabs and newlines, so `https://a.com/\r\nX: 1` passes validation. On redirect, `writeHead` throws on the invalid header character and the catch in src/app.js returns a 500. This is no header injection and no crash, but the link is accepted and then fails on every click. Rejecting control characters, or storing `new URL(value).href`, would fix it.
- `https:example.com` (no slashes) passes validation and is stored raw. Browsers handle it inconsistently, and it can resolve as a relative URL against an https base. Requiring `://`, or storing the normalised `.href`, would close this.
- Leading or trailing whitespace is accepted and stored unchanged."}

structured_output.riskNotes:
The change meets the issue. `isValidUrl` in src/url.js now parses the value and allows only the `http:` and `https:` protocols. The `javascript:`, `ftp:`, `data:` and `file:` schemes, bare hosts and non-string values all return 400 `{"error":"invalid url"}`. The new tests cover each of these, plus the mixed-case `JavaScript:` and `HTTPS://` cases and a check that a rejected URL isn't stored. I read the diff and ran small `node -e` checks; I didn't run `npm test` myself and relied on the verifier's pass. I found a few edge cases that don't block the merge.
- The raw `body.url` is stored, not the parsed or normalised form. WHATWG URL parsing strips embedded tabs and newlines, so `https://a.com/\r\nX: 1` passes validation. On redirect, `writeHead` throws on the invalid header character and the catch in src/app.js returns a 500. This is no header injection and no crash, but the link is accepted and then fails on every click. Rejecting control characters, or storing `new URL(value).href`, would fix it.
- `https:example.com` (no slashes) passes validation and is stored raw. Browsers handle it inconsistently, and it can resolve as a relative URL against an https base. Requiring `://`, or storing the normalised `.href`, would close this.
- Leading or trailing whitespace is accepted and stored unchanged.
